content.text:
This Annual Review covered the reporting period 2025-04-01 to 2026-03-31 under FCDO-funded programme MWI-EDU-AR-4471. The programme itself ran from 2024-10-15 to 2026-10-14, while the award letter stated that the first formal Annual Review period ran from 2024-10-15 to 2025-10-14. Submitted records therefore indicated a mismatch between the current report period label and the formal Year 1 review dates, and this should be read with that qualification.

At summary level, the programme remained aligned to its stated impact and outcome: adolescent girls in Machinga and Mangochi completing basic education in safer, more supportive learning environments, with improved retention, attendance and learning continuity and fewer practical and safeguarding barriers. However, verified actual results for the reporting period were not available in the submitted evidence pack used for this section. As a result, overall progress could not be rated here against output or outcome targets with confidence.

The approved FCDO contribution was GBP 1,240,000. The results framework set clear targets across attendance, retention, remedial learning, hardship support, menstrual health and hygiene support, safeguarding systems, learning products and district engagement. These included targets of 1,200 girls re-enrolled or newly retained, 900 supported girls attending at least 80% of school days in the last term, 850 girls completing at least 20 remedial learning sessions, 800 caregivers receiving a hardship grant linked to attendance, 1,100 girls receiving a re-entry kit or learning materials, 40 lockable girls' latrine stances rehabilitated or functional, 40 schools with menstrual supplies and trained focal teachers, 40 schools with an active safeguarding referral pathway tested, 8 district learning meetings with documented action points, 5 learning briefs produced and shared with stakeholders, and 240 school or community actors trained on re-entry and safeguarding. Outcome-level targets were also set at 70% for supported girls attending at least 80% of days in the last term, 65% progressing to the next grade or a re-entry pathway, and 72% reporting that school was safe during menstruation and travel.

The main issue for this section was not necessarily lack of programme activity but lack of verified performance data in the material provided here. The template required an Annual Review narrative, output scoring using the five-point system with evidence, a maintained logframe or equivalent results framework, and disaggregated monitoring data by gender, age and vulnerability where relevant. Those requirements were clear from the award documentation. Yet no confirmed output scores, actual indicator values, review team details or risk rating were available in the source set used for this summary. Exact disaggregation for girls with disabilities, ultra-poor households or out-of-school status was also not available here; the related equity reach indicator had no numeric target recorded.

On that basis, this summary recorded a cautious position. The programme had an approved scope, timeframe and target architecture in place, but this section could not confirm delivery against plan during 2025-04-01 to 2026-03-31 using verified actuals. The immediate recommendation was therefore to reconcile the reporting period basis with the formal Annual Review cycle stated in the award letter and complete the review pack with evidenced actual results, output scores, risk information and required disaggregation before final submission to FCDO.

content.text:
During the reporting period 2025-04-01 to 2026-03-31, the programme remained aligned to its stated outcome: adolescent girls targeted demonstrate improved school retention, attendance and learning continuity, with reduced practical and safeguarding barriers. The longer-term impact remained that adolescent girls in Machinga and Mangochi complete basic education in safer, more supportive learning environments. Reporting was prepared within the FCDO Annual Review framework for grant reference MWI-EDU-AR-4471.

Performance against expected results could only be assessed in a limited way from the submitted record. The available evidence confirmed the programme’s intended results framework and target values for key outcome and output indicators, but it did not include verified actual values for outcome indicators within this section’s source material. As a result, progress against the outcome could not be scored quantitatively here without overstating what the evidence showed.

The logframe direction of travel was clear. Outcome targets were set at 70% for supported girls attending at least 80% of school days in the last term, 65% for progression to the next grade or a re-entry pathway, and 72% for girls reporting that school was safe during menstruation and travel. Output targets also set the expected scale of delivery: 1,200 girls re-enrolled or newly retained; 900 girls attending at least 80% of school days in the last term; 850 girls completing at least 20 remedial learning sessions; 40 lockable girls’ latrine stances rehabilitated or functional; 40 schools with menstrual supplies and trained focal teachers; 40 schools with an active safeguarding referral pathway tested; 800 caregivers receiving a hardship grant linked to attendance; 1,100 girls receiving a re-entry kit or learning materials; 85% of hardship households receiving verified follow-up within 45 days; 8 district learning meetings with documented action points; 5 learning briefs produced and shared with stakeholders; and 240 school or community actors trained on re-entry and safeguarding.

These targets showed that delivery was designed to combine retention support, remedial learning, practical assistance, safer school conditions, safeguarding systems and district-level learning. That package remained coherent with the outcome statement. However, major deviations from expected results could not be confirmed from this evidence set because actual achievements, milestone tracking and verified variance explanations were not available in the submitted material used for this section.

On disaggregation, the award requirements stated that monitoring data must be disaggregated by gender, age and vulnerability. The proposal material also referenced reach to girls with disabilities, ultra-poor girls and out-of-school girls, but no numeric target was stated for that equity measure in the available record. The section therefore cannot report achieved disaggregation or equity reach figures with confidence. Exact disaggregation was not available in submitted records used here.

In conclusion, the programme had a clearly defined outcome pathway and a documented set of annual review obligations under FCDO requirements, including maintenance of a logframe or equivalent results framework and provision of output scoring with evidence. Based on the evidence available for this section, it is reasonable to conclude that performance management arrangements were specified, but actual progress against expected results during this reporting period was not evidenced strongly enough here to support a firm judgement on achievement level. The main lesson from this review stage is straightforward: future performance conclusions should draw directly on verified actuals, milestone status, output scores and disaggregated monitoring data so that variance against targets can be explained transparently.

content.text:
During the reporting period, the evidence base available for this Annual Review was limited and largely procedural rather than performance-focused. The programme operated within FCDO’s requirement to maintain a logframe or equivalent results framework, provide output scoring and evidence, and submit disaggregated monitoring data where relevant. However, the records provided for this section did not include verified indicator actuals, milestone tracking, or completed evaluation products that would allow a stronger assessment of progress against the results framework.

The strongest confirmed evidence in submitted records related to programme design parameters and reporting requirements rather than achieved results. The award documentation confirmed the formal reporting window for the first Annual Review as 15 October 2024 to 14 October 2025, while this draft report covered 2025-04-01 to 2026-03-31. That mismatch reduced confidence in assessing whether evidence had been assembled against the correct contractual review cycle. The same award documentation also confirmed that FCDO could request supporting documentation, which reinforced the expectation that underlying records should be available even where they were not included in the material reviewed for this section.

The existing results framework set out clear intended measures for attendance, progression or re-entry, safety, remedial learning, hardship support, school WASH and safeguarding conditions, and learning dissemination. For example, proposal targets referred to girls attending at least 80% of days in the last term, girls completing at least 20 remedial learning sessions, caregivers receiving hardship grants linked to attendance, schools with menstrual supplies and trained focal teachers, schools with tested safeguarding referral pathways, district learning meetings with documented action points, and learning briefs shared with stakeholders. These targets showed that an evaluable framework had been defined. Even so, no corresponding actual values were supplied in the records used here. As a result, this review could comment on evaluability but not on achieved performance.

On evidence quality, there was enough documentation to confirm that indicators and reporting obligations existed; there was not enough to verify delivery levels or outcome change. Evidence quality was therefore mixed: adequate for confirming planned indicators and compliance expectations, weak for judging actual results during the period under review. This mattered most for outcome-level assessment. Outcome statements referred to improved retention, attendance and learning continuity for adolescent girls in Machinga and Mangochi within safer and more supportive learning environments, but no monitored outcome values were available here to test whether those changes had occurred.

No new evaluation findings were evidenced in the submitted material reviewed for this section. Although the Annual Review pack was expected to include any evaluation or learning outputs, none were available in usable form within the present record set. For that reason, there was no basis to assess methodological quality of an evaluation study, triangulate monitoring data with independent inquiry, or judge whether emerging lessons had been validated beyond routine programme reporting.

Data quality limitations were significant. First, indicator actuals were absent across both output and outcome measures cited in programme documents. Second, while disaggregated monitoring data by gender, age and vulnerability was an explicit requirement, no disaggregated dataset or summary table was available in submitted records for this section. Third, one reporting-cycle reference in the award material mentioned an informal October-to-September convention, while the same document set out a formal first Annual Review period ending on 14 October 2025; this required careful handling and reduced certainty about which evidence window some internal references may have followed.

Taken together, the evidence base supported only a cautious conclusion: the programme had a defined theory of change and indicator structure acceptable for review purposes, but this section did not contain sufficient verified monitoring or evaluation material to substantiate claims on delivery quality or results achieved during 2025-04-01 to 2026-03-31.

content.text:
During the reporting period 2025-04-01 to 2026-03-31, risk reporting for the FCDO-funded programme MWI-EDU-AR-4471 was prepared against the Annual Review requirements set out in the award documentation. The programme maintained a logframe or equivalent results framework, and FCDO’s requirements included output scoring with supporting evidence, disaggregated monitoring data, and access to supporting documentation on request.

Submitted records did not provide a verified risk register update for this section. As a result, this review could not confirm which risks newly emerged, which assumptions materialised, or whether any individual risk rating changed during the period. It also could not present evidenced previous and current RAG ratings for the required risk update table without creating unsupported entries.

Safeguarding remained a core control issue within programme design and delivery. This was reflected in the results framework through targets linked to schools with active safeguarding referral pathways tested and school or community actors trained on re-entry and safeguarding. The outcome framework also tracked girls’ reported safety during menstruation and travel. These features showed that safeguarding risks were recognised within programme architecture. However, the submitted material for this section did not include confirmed incident data, trend analysis, case outcomes, or a documented statement on whether safeguarding risks increased, reduced, or remained stable over the review period.

The same evidence gap applied to fiduciary risk. No verified narrative was available on risks of funds not being used as intended, any control breaches identified during implementation, or corrective action taken during the period under review. Likewise, no confirmed section-specific evidence was provided on climate or environmental risk affecting delivery in Machinga and Mangochi.

Control expectations were clearer than control performance in the records available for drafting. FCDO required disaggregated monitoring data by gender, age and vulnerability where relevant, and retained the right to request supporting documents. Those requirements provided an accountability framework for oversight. Even so, exact evidence on compliance during this reporting period was not available in the submitted records for this section.

Overall, this section should be read as a constrained account based on award-level requirements and results-framework references rather than a fully evidenced risk update. A complete Annual Review narrative would require the underlying risk register, safeguarding reporting summary, and documented management actions from the reporting period.

sections.label: F. Programme Management: Delivery, Commercial and Financial Performance

content.text:
During the reporting period 2025-04-01 to 2026-03-31, programme management reporting for FCDO grant MWI-EDU-AR-4471 was framed against the formal award period from 2024-10-15 to 2026-10-14 and the requirement to submit an Annual Review pack, maintain a logframe or equivalent results framework, provide output scoring with evidence, and hold supporting documentation available on request. The submitted record therefore shows that management attention was directed to delivery assurance, results tracking and compliance with FCDO review requirements.

On delivery performance, the available evidence confirms the programme’s intended Impact and Outcome in Machinga and Mangochi, but it does not provide verified implementation data on partner performance, supplier or consultant performance, or completed activities during this section’s reporting window. Because actual delivery figures were not available in submitted records for this section, performance could not be tested here against output targets such as 1,200 girls re-enrolled or newly retained, 900 girls attending at least 80% of school days, 850 girls completing remedial sessions, 40 latrine stances rehabilitated or functional, 40 schools with menstrual supplies and trained focal teachers, 40 schools with tested safeguarding referral pathways, 800 caregivers receiving hardship grants, 1,100 girls receiving re-entry kits or learning materials, 8 district learning meetings, 5 learning briefs and 240 school or community actors trained. The same limitation applied to outcome-level targets on attendance, progression or re-entry, and perceived safety.

On financial performance, the only confirmed financial figure in the record was the approved FCDO contribution of GBP 1,240,000. No forecast-versus-actual spend data, burn rate data or variance analysis for the reporting period was available in the submitted evidence for this section. As a result, this review could not confirm whether expenditure tracked to plan during 2025-04-01 to 2026-03-31 or whether any underspend or overspend required corrective action.

On commercial performance, no verified procurement record, contract management update or supplier issue log was available in the evidence provided for this section. It was therefore not possible to confirm whether any commercial issues arose during implementation or whether supplier performance affected delivery.

On management actions and compliance with donor requirements, the record did show clear FCDO expectations: an Annual Review pack was due by 2025-11-21; monitoring data was expected to be disaggregated by gender, age and vulnerability; outputs were to be scored using a five-point system with supporting evidence; and FCDO retained the right to request supporting documents. These requirements established the management standard for the period. However, exact actions taken by FCDO or by implementing partners in response to delivery or financial issues were not evidenced in the material supplied for this section.

Overall, this section can confirm the programme’s management and accountability framework but cannot yet provide a fully evidenced judgement on delivery efficiency, commercial performance or financial execution for the reporting period because actual management data was not included in the submitted records.

This Annual Review recorded recommendations and action points, but the submitted evidence for this section was limited to placeholder gap responses rather than a completed action log. As a result, this section does not present verified recommendations from the review period. It instead notes that recommendations, updates on previous recommendations, and priorities for the next period were referenced in the reporting process but were not supplied in usable detail in the records reviewed.

For accountability purposes, the programme was expected to maintain a logframe or equivalent results framework, provide output scoring and evidence, and submit disaggregated monitoring data within the Annual Review pack. Those reporting requirements provided the basis on which recommendations should have been documented. However, no substantiated recommendation text, named owner, due date, priority level, status update, or follow-up action was available in the submitted material for this section.

The programme reference remained MWI-EDU-AR-4471 under FCDO funding. The formal first Annual Review period in the award documentation ran from 2024-10-15 to 2025-10-14, with the review pack due by 2025-11-21. The current report record covered 2025-04-01 to 2026-03-31, so there was a timing inconsistency between the report shell and the formal award-letter review cycle. That inconsistency should have been clarified in the action plan documentation, but no verified follow-up entry was available.

Because no evidence-backed recommendations table was provided, this section should be treated as incomplete pending submission of a populated recommendations and action points log.
